haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. The gateway makes no Redis call, so no counter is read or changed.

haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The request is never forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. The counter is not incremented on DENIED, so rejected requests use no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The counter is incremented before forwarding and never rolled back, so the request stays counted. The client gets the 500 with X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q6: The gateway forwards the request without retrying, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and adds no X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is NOT STATED; Product has not decided the number.

haiku-low.q10: The Lua script runs as one uninterrupted step on Redis, so the check and increment cannot be interleaved by another gateway.
haiku-low.q11: Retry-After is windowStart + 60 minus now, using the Redis clock, rounded up to whole seconds, minimum 1.
haiku-low.q12: No, the gateway does not retry the store. The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers, since the remaining count is unknown.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. No Redis call is made, so no counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: Limits belong to the customer and all its keys share one budget, so in total only the customer's single per-minute limit (e.g. 100/min on Standard).
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (integer seconds), and no X-RateLimit headers. The backend never sees the request.
sonnet.q4: No. On DENIED the counter is not incremented, so rejected requests use no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The counter was already incremented and is never rolled back, so the request stays counted even on a 500.
sonnet.q6: It fails open. The gateway forwards the request to the backend, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, adds no X-RateLimit headers, and does not retry.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is OPEN: Product has not decided the number, and the config has no Enterprise entry.
sonnet.q8: In a shared Redis counter with key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Each key gets a 120 s expiry, set when the count first becomes 1, which removes old counts.
sonnet.q9: When a new clock minute (window, by Redis's clock) starts, the count resets because a new counter key is used. A Redis key loss or restart also briefly gives a fresh budget.
sonnet.q10: The check and increment is one Lua script that Redis runs as a single uninterrupted step, so two gateways cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: It is windowStart + 60 - now, computed in the Lua script from Redis's clock, rounded up to whole seconds, minimum 1, as a plain integer.
sonnet.q12: No, it does not retry the store. The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers, because the remaining count is unknown, and otherwise sees a normal response.
